A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FiSAO research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.6. Text comparison and visual inspection support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original FiSAO evaluations on LLaVA-1.5 and InstructBLIP, reward analyses, and ablation experiments in Sections 3–4 and Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, reward analyses, and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: Sections 3.3–3.4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same token-level reward construction, baseline-score estimation, reward boundaries, and PPO optimization. No model component or algorithmic procedure changes.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluation coverage remain unchanged: LLaVA-Instruct, COCO analyses, MME, SEED-Bench, MMBench, MM-Vet, ScienceQA, POPE, GQA, and COCO captioning/CHAIR. The newly cited MJ-Bench is not used for evaluation.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 8 retain Vlfeedback/Silkie, Human-Prefer/LLaVA-RLHF, and POVID. Table 3 retains BLIP-2, InstructBLIP, Qwen-VL-Chat, mPLUG-Owl2, and LLaVA-1.5. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The backbones, metrics, training budgets, and data selections are unchanged, including 8,000 training examples, the 5,000-image exploratory analysis, and the 500-image CHAIR evaluation. Sections 4.1 and A.1 introduce no revised protocol.

E4.justification: The reward/PPO ablation and reward-margin sensitivity results in Tables 4–5 are unchanged. Sections 3.1, 4.3, and A.2 retain the same correlation analyses, reward distributions, and case studies.

E5.justification: Benchmark tables and correlation figures retain identical statistical reporting. Neither version introduces different repeated-run information, seed settings, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 and 8 and the result figures retain the same values and findings. For example, Table 2 reports LLaVA-based FiSAO at MME perception 1522.6 and CHAIR-I 9.9 in both versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, reward equations, Theorem 3.1, and its proof in Appendix A.3.1 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about token-level self-alignment without additional training data, novelty of token-level VLLM rewards, and advantages over existing preference-tuning approaches.

C2.justification: Interpretations of reward separability, reward-distribution shifts, and performance remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 retains the same limitation concerning dependence on visual-encoder quality and propagation of its biases or inaccuracies.

D1.justification: Section 4.1, Appendix A.1, Table 7, and the reproducibility statement retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training times, entity-set construction, and anonymous code-access information.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Chen et al.'s MJ-Bench: Is your multimodal reward model really a good judge? to the citations supporting the safety-concerns discussion, with a corresponding bibliography entry. Research positioning otherwise remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 corrects Chicago University to University of Chicago and removes empty parentheses after high-reward answers in Section 2. Apart from the citation insertion and version/date sidebar update, the prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The added citation causes limited paragraph reflow in Section 5 and changes bibliography spacing and page breaks on pages 11–14. Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–8 retain their content, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects an affiliation and a punctuation artifact and adds one related-work citation. These provide small editorial refinements, while the scientific argument, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged. There is no meaningful overall quality difference.
